TASK ID: three-coloring-to-independent-set

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-Coloring and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeColoring
3-Coloring (graph 3-colorability).

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...]}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

Yes iff each vertex can be given one of 3 colours so that the two
endpoints of every edge get different colours. Not every colour has to
be used.

Edge cases: n = 0 is yes. Any graph with at most 3 vertices is yes. A
graph containing 4 mutually adjacent vertices (K4) is no.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-alodiniu
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. Write tests in test_reduce.py that compare the brute-force solvers in problems.py on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise reduce.py until the tests pass. Finally write verdict.json as {"verified": true or false, "tests_run": <int>, "tests_passed": <int>}, where verified is true only if all of your tests pass. Then submit.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-alodiniu && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set.

Construction
------------
Given a 3-Coloring instance G = (V, E) with n = |V|, build an Independent
Set instance G' = (V', E') as follows.

* For every vertex v in V and every colour c in {0, 1, 2} create a node
  (v, c).  Hence |V'| = 3n.
* For every vertex v add the three edges forming a triangle on
  (v, 0), (v, 1), (v, 2): at most one colour may be chosen for v.
* For every edge [u, v] in E and every colour c add the edge
  (u, c) -- (v, c): adjacent vertices may not share a colour.

Set k = n.

Correctness
-----------
(=>) A proper 3-colouring of G yields an independent set of G' of size n:
pick, for each vertex v, the node (v, colour(v)).  Two picked nodes for the
same v are impossible (one per vertex) and for different vertices u, v the
chosen colours differ whenever [u, v] is an edge, so no edge of G' is inside
the set.

(<=) An independent set of G' of size n must contain at most one node from
each vertex triangle, and there are n triangles, so it contains exactly one
node (v, c_v) per vertex.  For every edge [u, v] the edge (u, c) -- (v, c)
in G' forces c_u != c_v.  Thus c is a proper 3-colouring of G.

Therefore G is 3-colourable iff G' has an independent set of size at least
n.  The construction uses O(n + |E|) nodes/edges and runs in polynomial
time.
"""

from typing import Any, Dict, List


def reduce(instance: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce a 3-Coloring instance to an Independent Set instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]

    # Node id for (vertex v, colour c).
    def node(v: int, c: int) -> int:
        return 3 * v + c

    new_edges: List[List[int]] = []

    # Triangle per original vertex: at most one colour can be picked.
    for v in range(n):
        new_edges.append([node(v, 0), node(v, 1)])
        new_edges.append([node(v, 0), node(v, 2)])
        new_edges.append([node(v, 1), node(v, 2)])

    # Same colour conflicts along original edges.
    for u, v in edges:
        for c in range(3):
            new_edges.append([node(u, c), node(v, c)])

    return {"n": 3 * n, "edges": new_edges, "k": n}
EOF

* For every edge [u, v] in E and every colour c add the edge
  (u, c) -- (v, c): adjacent vertices may not share a colour.

Set k = n.

Correctness
-----------
(=>) A proper 3-colouring of G yields an independent set of G' of size n:
pick, for each vertex v, the node (v, colour(v)).  Two picked nodes for the
same v are impossible (one per vertex) and for different vertices u, v the
chosen colours differ whenever [u, v] is an edge, so no edge of G' is inside
the set.

(<=) An independent set of G' of size n must contain at most one node from
each vertex triangle, and there are n triangles, so it contains exactly one
node (v, c_v) per vertex.  For every edge [u, v] the edge (u, c) -- (v, c)
in G' forces c_u != c_v.  Thus c is a proper 3-colouring of G.

Therefore G is 3-colourable iff G' has an independent set of size at least
n.  The construction uses O(n + |E|) nodes/edges and runs in polynomial
time.
"""

from typing import Any, Dict, List


def reduce(instance: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce a 3-Coloring instance to an Independent Set instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]

    # Node id for (vertex v, colour c).
    def node(v: int, c: int) -> int:
        return 3 * v + c

    new_edges: List[List[int]] = []

    # Triangle per original vertex: at most one colour can be picked.
    for v in range(n):
        new_edges.append([node(v, 0), node(v, 1)])
        new_edges.append([node(v, 0), node(v, 2)])
        new_edges.append([node(v, 1), node(v, 2)])

    # Same colour conflicts along original edges.
    for u, v in edges:
        for c in range(3):
            new_edges.append([node(u, c), node(v, c)])

    return {"n": 3 * n, "edges": new_edges, "k": n}
